liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Desolation Row** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer believes Weir helped Dylan through most of the lyrics; crowd responded loudly when Dylan sang; Dylan and Weir together on Desolation Row was interesting [4][19][26]
- **I Can't Get No Satisfaction** (2 reviews): Satisfaction was a highlight, though reviewer also thought the second half of the second set rocked; Only Satisfaction worth keeping, because of the band member announcements [16][25]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Ramble On Rose as opener was sweet; Dylan joined to close the first set on Baby Blue and Desolation Row [23]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Playin' jam is short but strong, with Phil and Bob taking over after Jerry and Brent left the stage [24]
- Dylan goes around introducing the band members during Satisfaction [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-07-07.158834.aud.nak300s.carpenter.flac2448** (recommended): audience recording; 16 songs; 107 min [1]
- **gd1986-07-07.fm.miller.88176.flac16**: FM broadcast; 15 songs; 111 min; rated 3.74/5 by 19 [2]. Said about its sound: Some FM static in Box Of Rain and Wharf Rat; uploader cleaned up as much as possible [2]
- **gd86-07-07.schoeps.conner.7001.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 15 songs; 107 min; rated 2.67/5 by 27 [8]
- **gd1986-07-07.135066.chasingwilma.flac24**: source not stated; 15 songs; 111 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer found the rest of the performance strange and mediocre, with Jerry seriously ill [15]
- Jerry, visibly sick, repeatedly left the stage during the second set; reviewer found the performance uninspired, and he fell into a coma days later [17]
- Weather was extremely hot; the Dead's first set was very short, four songs, including two mellow Dylan songs with Dylan [18]
- Jerry had a fever from an abscessed tooth yet played well; a strong jam followed his exit after Terrapin [19]
- Reviewer says Jerry was in bad shape, with weak vocals and a short show [21]
- Last show before Jerry's coma; his voice was scraggly but he soloed well in both sets [24]
- Reviewer found the first set only five songs and Dylan's stage appearance on the last two songs embarrassing [25]
- Very hot, around 103 degrees; crowd was hosed down. Dylan and Petty opened, and Petty's Heartbreakers mini-set was great [26]
- Reviewer says many 1986 shows felt strange and were short, but this one was the worst [17]
- Summer 1986 stadium shows were shortened for Dylan/Petty sets, which sometimes opened and sometimes followed the Dead [18]
- Weather was cooler than the previous day, which reviewer considered a weaker show; crowd was smaller, and it was a Monday [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-07-07.158834.aud.nak300s.carpenter.flac2448**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Ted Carpenter; source: Nak 300s /w cp4s - TCD5M no Dolby Maxell XL-IIS 90s [1]. Also: First set complete; The Other One patched to cover a tape flip, with gain raised 2 dB [1]
- **gd1986-07-07.fm.miller.88176.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: In-House FM -> FM Receiver -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D6C/Denon HD-M90) D [2]. Also: Schoeps CMC3/MK4 to PCM to DAT to CD; masters lent by Dan Gale [2]
- **gd86-07-07.schoeps.conner.7001.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Connor; source: Audience: Schoeps mk4/cmc3 [8]. Also: Reviewer has a partial high-generation tape of a soundboard of this show [24]
- **gd1986-07-07.135066.chasingwilma.flac24**: taped by Unknown; transferred by chasingwilma; source: lineage: sennheiser 421 fob> tcd-d5> mc > c> sony tc we435> sony pcm m-10 24bit/96khz> soundforge> cdwave> traders little helper encoding option 8 [3]
